purpose: Confirmatory replication of R2_DEADLINE_TESTBED with a deadline corrected after R2: the R2 primary deadline missed on D0 (zero network slack; host overhead not in the formula) and fell short of 99% on D4 (per-leg p99 instead of the quantile of the t-th arrival). The corrected deadline is fixed here from the R2b calibration and the order-statistic model, and tested on fresh traces.
result_blind_statement: R2 outcomes were known when this was designed and motivated it; no R2b trace existed. The deadline uses only the calibration run and frozen parameters.

testbed.label: SINGLE_HOST_EMULATION_REAL_CRYPTO_NOT_FIELD_DATA
testbed.topology: 32 custodian OS processes, each an asyncio TCP server on 127.0.0.1 holding only its own share; one combiner process (asyncio client) that issues requests, verifies DLEQ proofs as responses arrive, stops at t valid, combines, unwraps the record key and AES-GCM-decrypts Proof verification runs off the combiner event loop (worker thread or process).
testbed.network_emulation: one-way delay per message drawn by the combiner-side emulator from the trace seed and passed as out-of-band emulation metadata; the custodian sleeps the inbound delay before computing and the outbound delay before replying; lost messages are never answered; no retransmission
testbed.delay_model: lognormal one-way delay with stated median and sigma (log-space); 0 means no injected delay

committee.keygen: dealer keygen once per profile run

testbed.crypto: ristretto255; dispute partials use TDH2 with label (epoch, record id, policy hash); audit uses beacon-derived canary
testbed.crash_selection: crashed members chosen uniformly per trace from the trace seed; domain outage = one domain chosen uniformly per trace, all 8 members silent
testbed.trace_seed: int.from_bytes(SHA256('KEYSTONE-R2B|DEADLINE|' + profile_id + '|' + str(i))[:8], 'big'), identical for both variants (paired)

variants.SERIAL: primary: serial verification on arrival, stop at t valid
variants.BATCH: secondary: verify arrivals in batches by random linear combination; fall back to individual verification on batch failure

primary_endpoint: Pr[dispute decrypts the correct plaintext by Delta_os(profile)], SERIAL, per reconstructable profile; for D5-GLOBAL-CRASH11 (no Delta_os) success at any time
criterion: a reconstructable profile meets the endpoint if the 95% Wilson upper bound of its success rate is at least 0.99; D5 is expected at 0%
secondary_endpoints: paired SERIAL vs BATCH: exact two-sided McNemar test on success by Delta_os; paired completion-time difference (median and exact sign test) over traces where both succeed
model check: predicted vs observed success at the R2 deadline Delta_d_star and at Delta_os (prediction inside the Wilson interval)
success at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 s; completion-time median and p95
audit pass rate versus exact expectation
interval_method: Wilson 95% for proportions; order-statistic quantiles for times
pre_stated_expectation: success by Delta_os at or near 99% in every reconstructable profile, 0% in D5; no material SERIAL vs BATCH difference; reported whatever the outcome
claim_boundary: single host, synthetic delay laws; a replication, not field data
